title: China Might Lap the United States on AI Adoption
gist: Thibaut and Duffy contrast Washington's exclusive 'full-stack' AI export strategy (Pax Silica, American AI Exports Program) with Beijing's inclusive development offer built around open-weight models, training and the new Shanghai-based WAICO. They argue first-mover advantage in global AI adoption will go to whoever best integrates infrastructure, models, financing and capacity building while letting partners mix and match, and Beijing is currently better positioned.

insights.claim: Washington's AI diplomacy bundles advanced chips, cloud, models, compute, applications and financing into a 'full-stack' export package featuring US industry and offered to favored nations, aimed at winning an AI race with China.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: US AI exporters' overseas growth is tied to government-curated packages and alignment criteria.

insights.claim: Beijing's AI diplomacy promotes locally owned and operated, locally adapted AI models backed by training, capacity building, a new multilateral body and Chinese applications, emphasizing equitable access for middle- and low-income countries.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: China's offer targets the large Global South market where US premium AI is less affordable.

insights.claim: Washington is implementing its multilateral AI offer through Pax Silica, which aims to secure AI supply chains and has about two dozen partner signatories, and through the American AI Exports Program that gives US consortia priority federal financing and export-license processing.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: US AI companies in approved consortia gain preferential financing and licensing for foreign sales.

insights.claim: No US program offers a development-oriented soft-power AI package comparable to China's, and the US has expressly rejected any independent multilateral body for AI governance or cooperation.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: A gap in US offerings leaves room for Chinese vendors in developing-country public-sector AI.
insights.quote: While the U.S. approach offers components of an AI ecosystem strategy, no U.S. program creates a soft-power offering similar to China’s development offerings.

themes.theme: WAICO and China's AI development offer

insights.claim: In July, representatives of 29 countries signed an agreement establishing the World AI Cooperation Organization (WAICO) as an intergovernmental body headquartered in Shanghai, with more countries reportedly joining since.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: China now has a standing multilateral vehicle to steer AI standards and procurement in partner states.

insights.claim: Xi Jinping pledged 5,000 AI training and seminar opportunities for developing countries over five years, AI application centers with BRICS, ASEAN, the African Union and the Arab League, and help for 30 countries to use China's AI-powered Mazu early-warning system.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: Concrete commitments seed Chinese AI tooling familiarity across emerging-market governments.
insights.quote: Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged 5,000 AI training and seminar opportunities for developing countries over five years.

insights.claim: WAICO's July announcement did not specify a financing mechanism, a delivery structure, or how the body's independence would be assured, so its practical impact remains unclear and Chinese announcements still outpace implementation.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: Execution risk tempers the threat China's AI diplomacy poses to US vendors in the near term.

insights.claim: Open-weight models let developers copy and adapt AI without training from scratch, making systems cheaper and especially useful for nations needing systems tailored to local environments, which is central to China's AI development plan.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: Open-weight economics favor Chinese models in cost-sensitive markets.

insights.claim: The ASEAN-China AI Industry Innovation Center, inaugurated in Beijing on May 24, pairs AI demonstrations in healthcare and agriculture with training for ASEAN officials, employees and students.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
entities: ASEAN-China Artificial Intelligence Industry Innovation Center
insights.so_what: Southeast Asia is an early testbed for China's bundled AI-plus-training model.

insights.claim: China's World Artificial Intelligence Conference featured more than 3,000 exhibits from over 1,100 companies, displaying the industrial breadth that could underpin Chinese AI applications.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: Indicates the depth of China's AI application vendor base.
insights.quote: With more than 3,000 exhibits from over 1,100 companies, the WAIC displayed the industrial breadth that could underpin Chinese AI applications.

insights.claim: Reuters reported a draft State Department letter saying Pax Silica membership could not be held alongside membership in duplicative initiatives, signaling Washington may force partners to choose between US and Chinese AI frameworks.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: Forced-choice alignment could fragment AI markets into blocs and complicate multinational AI deployment.

insights.claim: Forcing governments to choose between the US and China is unlikely to win the AI race because governments want to combine American and Chinese AI technologies and avoid dependency on any single nation's stack, especially as allies' trust in the US is at all-time lows.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: Hybrid US-China AI stacks abroad would limit US vendors' ability to lock in markets.
insights.quote: It is hard to see how the U.S. can “win” any AI race by forcing governments around the world to choose between the two leading powers.
insights.locator: It is hard to see how

insights.claim: On Sept. 14, ECB President Christine Lagarde warned that reliance on foreign AI raises questions about whose laws govern sensitive data and whether access to essential services could be withdrawn or used as political leverage.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: European sovereignty concerns support demand for local or diversified AI infrastructure.

insights.claim: On Sept. 21, Finland, Norway, 19 other nations and the European Commission issued a joint statement urging global collaboration on frontier AI risks, with signatories spanning Pax Silica members, WAICO participants and nonaligned states.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: Cross-bloc demand for multilateral AI governance undercuts exclusive alignment strategies.

insights.claim: First-mover advantage in global AI will go not to the country with the most cutting-edge models but to the one that best integrates infrastructure, models, applications, financing, capacity building and standards into a coherent offering partners can mix and match.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: Frontier-model leadership may not translate into international market share for AI vendors.
insights.quote: First-mover advantages won’t go to the AI leader with the most cutting-edge models.

insights.claim: Early training programs shape local engineers' familiarity with specific software and hardware, and procurement rules set early determine which AI technologies can be deployed, creating durable lock-in for whoever moves first.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: Capacity-building programs are a leading indicator of future AI vendor share in emerging markets.
insights.quote: Training programs will shape local engineers’ familiarity with specific software or hardware tools

insights.claim: Any bilateral US-China AI safety agreement would undercut Washington's ability to demand partners avoid AI collaboration with China, while challenging Beijing's inclusion narrative by excluding other nations.
insights.speaker: Kenton Thibaut, Kat Duffy
insights.so_what: A US-China AI deal would loosen alignment pressure on third countries, benefiting Chinese AI exporters.
insights.locator: The world is waiting to see
